notes.statuses: doc_verify_facts checks a candidate's shape (value_schema; a wrong shape is rejected, check value), that its quote is on the cited page (rejected, check quote), every part under checked (a part the quote does not state is needs_review, check consistency), its confidence (below 0.8: needs_review, check confidence), and then that every other part is confirmed: a part under checked_if_written that the quote does not write out, or any part under always_review, holds the candidate in needs_review with check coverage. Verified means every part of the value was confirmed.
notes.paths: Paths start at value; [] stands for every item of an array. form string or object marks the two shapes of a predicate that also accepts a plain summary string.
notes.confirmation: A person who has read the clause can confirm the parts no quote can prove: send the candidate again with confirmation {by, at, note?}. by is the person's name or role; FactLot records it as given and does not authenticate it, so an agent must never confirm its own extraction. The fact is then verified with method human_verified, the quote-checked parts under checked and the rest under confirmed_by_person. A confirmation never overrides a quote that is not on the page, a part under checked that the quote does not state, or a low confidence.
notes.generic: Any other dotted lower_snake predicate (lease.notice_days, om.occupancy) is accepted with generic rules: the value must not be null or blank; every number, ratio (a number in (0, 1]) and date in it is checked against the quote, and text counts as checked only when written in the quote.

alternate_forms.how: A rent table written by lease year (Lease Years 1–5: $34.50 ...). Give steps {lease_years: [first, last], annual_rent_psf} and, on the candidate, commencement {value, quote, page}. FactLot checks each rent and each lease-year number against the table's quote and the commencement date against its own quote, then derives each step's from and to: Lease Year N runs from the (N−1)th anniversary of the commencement date to the day before the next (a February 29 commencement's anniversary in a common year is February 28). The verified fact cites both quotes, keeps lease_years on each step, names formula doc.lease_year_dates@1, and the result shows the dates under derived_from. If the commencement date is not verified, the schedule stays in needs_review (check derivation).
